recommendations.summary: GEOMETRIC-GROWTH MAXIMISATION of the discretionary sleeve. Principal: 'max geometric growth and heavy compounding, definitely earning 100-200-300 net CAGR.' Three levers, each raising E[log wealth] rather than raising bet size. (1) CALIBRATION-DRIVEN SIZING: the sizer trusted Claude's STATED probability. If it claims 0.63 and truly hits 0.45 that is ~2x Kelly, where growth is NEGATIVE -- no edge survives systematically over-betting it. Size now uses the MEASURED calibration, both directions: a desk found under-confident gets its size RAISED automatically. The raw claim is still what gets scored, or the correction would launder the model's error and the bias would stop being measurable. (2) HEAT HEADROOM AS A SIZER, not a gate: a busy book now TRIMS a good setup instead of refusing it, because an unbooked setup contributes exactly zero to growth. Solved against EFFECTIVE heat, so an uncorrelated trade gets far more room than a duplicate -- multivariate Kelly made operational (on a 5-alt book, gold gets 4.39pct vs LTC 3.14pct). (3) GROWTH IS NOW MEASURED: log-growth per trade, realised trades/year, implied CAGR, and -- the part that matters -- the BINDING CONSTRAINT named as EDGE or FREQUENCY, because if g<=0 raising cadence multiplies a losing bet.

recommendations.summary: THE DISCRETIONARY DESK AS A FIRST-CLASS SECTION, with a learning loop. Principal: 'train the brain to maximum to get better and more profitable at these... just as much priority as the other section... minimum consistent 300 net CAGR... this should all be BINANCE, don't mistake it for MT5.' VENUE CORRECTED throughout: the sleeve trades Binance USD-M perps; the MT5 screenshots were the origin of the idea and one data point on trail width, never the venue. run_trade_review.py reads each closed trade against what was claimed at entry and classifies the cause into something actionable (THESIS-WRONG / LEVEL-WRONG / TIMING-WRONG / NOISE-STOP / RIGHT-AND-PAID / RIGHT-BUT-TRUNCATED / UNLUCKY -- that last one load-bearing, since a desk that cannot tell right-and-unlucky from wrong will 'fix' a working process), then extracts ONE falsifiable lesson. The playbook is an EVIDENCE LADDER: PROVISIONAL on one observation with no authority, SUPPORTED after 3 agreeing trades, RETIRED the moment one contradicts it with the contradiction recorded, STALE after 25 untested trades. Only SUPPORTED lessons reach the brief. Outcomes are also CONDITIONED ON SETUP (trend alignment, vol regime, position in range, level touches, horizon) because one global hit rate hides everything actionable -- 55pct with the 4h trend and 25pct against reads as a mediocre 40pct, and the fix is invisible until it is split. docs/DISCRETIONARY_DESK.md states the section, its organs, its method and what 300pct actually requires: a ~38pct hit rate against a 31.1pct cost-adjusted breakeven.

recommendations.summary: COPYTRADING SCREENED, Stage A, zero promotion authority. Two hypotheses, opposite verdicts. H1 FOLLOW A LEAD TRADER: ABANDONED as untestable from public data. The naive split-half test on 34 OKX lead traders returns Spearman +0.33 with 5/6 of the top quintile beating the median -- and it is an artifact: cohort SELECTED ON THE OUTCOME (sorted by pnl/aum/copiers/winRatio then measured for performance), blown-up traders absent entirely so persistence is manufactured by the survival filter, mean 45d return +81pct across the sample (a leaderboard, not a population), n=34 giving ~1.9 sigma BEFORE either bias. Economics add a 13pct copier profit share, entry lag behind the lead, and the lead's full drawdown. H2 TRADE THE COPY FLOW: KEPT and measured. Copy capital is FORCED flow -- copiers enter behind the lead, exit when it exits, liquidate together -- so aggregate skew and stress are a crowding gauge needing no winner picked, which is exactly why it dodges the selection problem. Live: 164 positions, median leverage 20x, 52pct underwater. Screen archives a FORWARD PANEL counting disappearances as FAILURES, the only unbiased design; NO-DATA until two snapshots sit 5+ days apart. Judged against max E[log wealth]: a sleeve adding only crypto beta adds ~nothing, so any promotion must show DIVERSIFYING return.
recommendations.reason: Stage A run live; H1 abandoned on measurement, H2 on a forward clock

recommendations.summary: CALIBRATION PROBE -- test the load-bearing assumption under the entire discretionary sizer: that the model's stated probability means anything. Kelly is f*=(pb-q)/b, so if p is noise the sizer is not aggressive or conservative, it is ARBITRARY. Checked 2026-07-31: the desk had ZERO resolved forecasts. Not few -- zero. The most consequential input to the money path had never been scored on anything, and both trading sleeves were built to consume it. Calibration is a property of the FORECASTER, not of the strategy, so it is measurable TODAY with questions that resolve from public price data in hours: no capital, no venue keys, ~50 forecasts in two days at the cost of quota alone. Poses 6 directional questions every 6h on the sleeve's own instruments -- the same KIND of judgement it makes when trading, so the measured calibration transfers -- and resolves anything due from real bars. Pre-committed verdict: Brier >= 0.25 (the score of always answering 50%) means REMOVE the Kelly sizer and run flat size, because sizing on a meaningless number is strictly worse than not sizing on it.
recommendations.reason: built, 8 tests, every 6h; feeds L1.29 which the conviction sizer already reads

recommendations.summary: 2-OF-3 ENSEMBLE CONSENSUS on the conviction sleeve -- buy hit rate with frequency. Correct only because of WHERE the hit rate sits: cost-adjusted breakeven is 31.1pct and the plausible rate is on top of it, so g per trade is tiny and small precision gains multiply it (32->33pct is x3.5 on g, 32->36pct is x11) while halving the trade count costs a factor of 2. Through the honest haircuts: no filter 33pct/460 = 34pct CAGR; 2-of-3 at 36pct/230 = 58pct; at 38pct/230 = 95pct. Three reads framed DIFFERENTLY (straight / argue the opposite side / assume your instinct is already priced) because three samples of one framing correlate and their agreement means nothing. 2-of-3 not unanimity, which cuts to ~1/4 the trades for +8pp and measures 63pct against 95pct. Consensus takes the LOWEST probability among agreeing reads since Kelly is convex in p. The rejected minority is KEPT so whether the filter helps stays measurable -- if agreement-filtered calls do not out-hit unfiltered ones, the filter goes.

Also CORRECTS gap #71's premise: switching the screen from Romano-Wolf FWER to Benjamini-Hochberg buys no power for the single best candidate, because BH's rank-1 threshold is q/m -- Bonferroni exactly -- and screen_select is wired with method='by', which is stricter still by H_m=6.6. So leaving CampaignGates.screen unwired costs nothing today; rewiring it would add false names without lowering the floor.

recommendations.summary: Gauntlet audit: the multiplicity penalty was paid TWICE and that, not any threshold, is why nothing survived. DSR is a Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio against a DEFLATED benchmark sr0=expected_max_sharpe(n_trials); that deflation IS a multiplicity correction over the campaign, and on the per-candidate path Romano-Wolf already controls family-wise error over the SAME N candidates. Two family-wise bars were compounded into one nothing could pass. MEASURED on 240 genuine alphas and ~4,800 nulls per effect size (N=420, T=310), scoring through the real validate(): power at true Sharpe 2.0 was 0.0%, at 3.0 it was 1.2%. Gate subsets at SR=5: all gates 5.8% power / 0.000% FPR; WITHOUT DSR 83.8% power / 0.000% FPR; without reality_check 5.8% (masked by DSR); without BOTH 100% power / 32.3% FPR -- so exactly one correction is needed, not zero and not two. Leave-one-out alone could never have found this because DSR masks reality_check. The corrections are correctly SIZED as family-wise tests (White 3.3%, SPA 5.0%, Romano-Wolf 5.0% against nominal 5%) -- the defect was controlling family-wise error twice over one family, not miscalibration. Discrimination was always fine (DSR AUC 0.980 at SR=3), which is the signature of a good statistic behind an unreachable threshold. ADVERSARIAL CHECK that could have overturned it: PSR adjusts for skew/kurtosis and Romano-Wolf does not, so DSR might have been catching negatively-skewed nulls -- tested on a short-vol true null (skew -6.15, kurtosis 45.6) and FPR was IDENTICAL at 0.150% with and without DSR. The argument did not survive measurement. FIX: on the per-candidate path DSR is computed with n_trials=1, removing the duplicated deflation and RETAINING the moment-aware PSR; the legacy path keeps full deflation because nothing else corrects there. Power 0.0->5.83% at SR=2 and 1.2->23.75% at SR=3, false positives 0/5040 -> 1/5040 (overlapping 95% intervals). No threshold lowered: _DSR_THRESHOLD is still 0.95 and Romano-Wolf still holds FWER at 5%. BOTTLENECK, separately: history length moves power (T=310/620/1250/2500 -> 0.00/1.67/4.58/19.58% at SR=2) and campaign size does NOT (N=420/100/30 all 0.00%), while the campaign discards 82.9% of the observations it already has via min-length truncation (310 retained of 1808 available per candidate).
recommendations.reason: n_trials=1 on the per-candidate path removes the duplicated deflation and retains the moment-aware PSR; legacy path keeps full deflation. Post-fix power 0.0/0.0/1.2/12.1/40.4% -> 1.67/5.83/23.75/85.42/100.00% at true Sharpe 1.5/2/3/5/7, false positives 0/5040 -> 1/5040 with overlapping 95% intervals. The bottleneck finding (history length, not campaign size; 82.9% of observations discarded by min-length truncation) is NOT addressed by this commit and is the larger remaining lever.

recommendations.summary: Min-length truncation PRICED: it is the largest remaining loss in the discovery pipeline, and a stratification planner now quantifies it. Every campaign builder aligns its matrix with min_len = min(len(r) for r in return_series), so ONE short candidate truncates every other -- 310 observations retained of ~1,808 available per candidate, 82.9% of the data on disk discarded before a single test ran. That is exactly backwards given the audit: observations buy power (T=310/620/1250/2500 -> 0.0/1.7/4.6/19.6% at true Sharpe 2) and cohort size does not (N=420/100/30 all 0.0%). libs/validation/campaign_window.py partitions candidates by AVAILABLE HISTORY via an exact DP so every candidate is tested at the longest window it can support and none is truncated to a stranger's. On a realistic length distribution: expected discoveries 1.06 -> 159.0, observations used 18.0% -> 89.0%, candidates tested 420 -> 326 (the rest are too short to reach the floors). TWO SELF-INFLICTED DEFECTS CAUGHT DURING THE BUILD, both recorded in code. (1) The first objective maximised per-candidate power and chose 4,000 obs x 16 candidates -- 99.9% power with 404 of 420 hypotheses never tested; a dropped candidate has ZERO discovery probability, not a small one, so the objective became expected discoveries = cohort x power summed over strata. (2) The unpriced version then fragmented into 34 minimum-size strata because smaller cohorts carry a smaller multiplicity deflation -- evading the correction by partitioning, and it would have reported a fictional 279x. Each stratum is now scored at CAMPAIGN_ALPHA/k so total family-wise error stays 5% however the campaign is cut. MAX_STRATA was also set from a sweep (optimum k=26) after an initial guess of 8 sat hard against the cap. NOT WIRED, deliberately: romano_wolf_stepdown takes alpha=0.05 and no builder passes anything else, so a k-stratum campaign today would run k families at 5% each and the real FWER would be ~1-(1-0.05)^k. The Bonferroni accounting is a property of the CALLER; wiring the plan without wiring the level would turn a measured improvement into a genuine loosening. 10 tests.
recommendations.reason: libs/validation/campaign_window.py prices the loss: expected discoveries 1.06 -> 159.0, observations used 18.0% -> 89.0% on a realistic length distribution. Split priced at CAMPAIGN_ALPHA/k so total FWER stays 5% however the campaign is cut; MAX_STRATA set from a sweep (optimum k=26) after a guess of 8 sat against the cap; 10 tests including results-blindness of the planner. DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED -- romano_wolf_stepdown takes alpha=0.05 and no builder passes otherwise, so the Bonferroni accounting is a property of the caller. Wiring the plan without wiring the level is the follow-up and is tracked separately.

NOT transferable and must not be pretended: colocation, market-making at scale, a research headcount. Also flag the honest tension: Medallion is 100 percent systematic with zero discretion, so the conviction sleeve is structurally anti-Medallion -- principal decision, not the desk s.

GENERALISE THE RULE (proactive battery move 6): the gap register carries the SAME defect class fixed in the carry-over brief today, and its prior triage rejected the fix on an objection the new design answers. rerank_gaps.py:109 takes worst = min(deadlines) over every date in a row, so an ORIGINAL missed deadline permanently dominates any later deferral -- rows #70/#74/#75 were re-deferred to 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-19 by the 08-04 cycle and still print DEADLINE-PASSED today, exactly as libs/ops/carryover.py:181 printed a defect fixed 7 times as 'shown the work and not done'. THE PRIOR CYCLE'S OBJECTION WAS SOUND AND IS NOW OBSOLETE: it declined to clear the flag because 'overwriting the passed date erases the fact that the desk missed it -- the denominator trick section 34 forbids'. Correct, and that is precisely why min() is the wrong operator rather than the right one: the fix is NOT to overwrite the miss but to report BOTH facts, which is strictly more information than either alone. Design, mirroring the carry-over fix shipped this cycle: rank on the CURRENT (latest) deadline, and carry missed_deadlines as its own distinct field, so a row renders 'DEFERRED 2026-08-12 (1 deadline missed)' instead of a permanent DEADLINE-PASSED that cannot be cleared by any honest act. Preserves the full history, keeps the treadmill visible via the miss COUNT (a row on its fourth re-deferral is louder under this scheme, not quieter), and restores the register's ability to distinguish parked from re-committed. Cheap: one operator change, one field, one render line, plus tests asserting a re-deferred row shows its miss count and a never-deferred overdue row is unchanged. Precedent and test pattern: tests/ops/test_carryover.py::TestRecurrenceIsNotASkip.

This is not confined to one odd ticker -- 1000PEPEUSDT and 1000SHIBUSDT are liquid Binance perps and fail identically, so the probe organ can silently lose any digit-bearing name it draws. EXACT PATCH: widen the three character classes from [A-Z]{2,12} to [A-Z0-9]{2,12}; the USD[TC]? suffix still anchors the match, and a bare decimal like '102.0 USD' cannot match it. VERIFY BEFORE CLAIMING: run score_forecasts.py dry-run and confirm the 44 move from SKIPPED to resolvable, then --write and confirm check_calibration leaves OVERDUE. NOTE THE SIZING CONSEQUENCE, which is why this is not a pure cleanup: resolving these moves report()'s bias, which calibrated_confidence feeds to kelly_leverage in run_conviction_trader -- the duplicate-claim exclusion in _scoreable collapses the 44 identical S2USDT claims to ONE observation, which is the designed behaviour and should be confirmed rather than assumed. Found while building R0123's decline grader, which is the adjacent path and is NOT the cause: the grader's 6 new rows resolved in-pass and left overdue at 44 unchanged.

LEDGER WRITES RE-ENCODE ~40 UNRELATED ROWS ON EVERY APPEND, making the one file two writers share unreviewable. scripts/recommendations.py:69 does json.dumps(d, indent=1) with ensure_ascii at its default True, but docs/research/recommendation_ledger.json was previously written with non-ASCII preserved. So the first recommendations.py write after any other writer flips every em-dash, section sign, arrow and CJK character in the file to a \\uXXXX escape -- measured 2026-08-05: a single 'add' produced a 104-line diff of which ~40 lines were pure re-encoding of rows nobody touched, burying the two real changes. Three costs, all real: (1) a reviewer cannot see what actually changed, which is how a bad disposition slips through; (2) the churn maximises merge-conflict surface on a file the desk has ALREADY corrupted once (R0175) and which parallel agents are told to treat as read-only precisely because it has no locking; (3) it oscillates -- whichever writer runs last wins, so the diff noise recurs indefinitely rather than settling. EXACT PATCH: json.dumps(d, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) at scripts/recommendations.py:69, then one normalising commit that rewrites the file in that encoding so the escapes are gone for good. CHECK FIRST whether any other writer of this file also needs the flag (grep for recommendation_ledger.json writers) -- fixing one of two writers leaves the oscillation in place, which is the failure mode that makes this look fixed while it is not.

A DISPOSITION'S --commit SHA IS SILENTLY INVALIDATED BY ANY REBASE, AND THERE IS NO VERB TO RE-POINT IT. Hit live 2026-08-05: three rows were disposed implemented citing a4054a8/5b0cb81/3abe48b, then the branch had to be rebased onto origin (a sibling had pushed 13 commits to the same branch). Rebase rewrote all three SHAs. The cited commits survive only as orphaned local objects until gc and NEVER reach the remote, so the ledger's proof-of-work pointed at commits no other clone can resolve -- a false citation in exactly the dimension the --commit field exists to make true, and one that gets WORSE with time rather than announcing itself. scripts/recommendations.py:172 correctly refuses to re-dispose ('dispositions do not revert') and offers only 'correct', which re-OPENS the row and files the prior disposition as MISFILED. That is the wrong shape here: the disposition was right, only the pointer moved, and recording it as a misfiling would corrupt the correction history that verb exists to protect. Worked around this time by a surgical edit of the three commit fields, matching recommendations.py:69's exact serialization so the diff stayed at 6 lines. FIX, one of: (a) add a 'repoint --id --commit --reason' verb, which mutates only the commit field and appends to a repoints[] list -- cheap and exact; or (b) have dispose resolve the sha to a stable form at write time; or (c) a fence that walks implemented rows and reports any commit not reachable from the remote-tracking branch, which also catches the pre-existing rows nobody re-pointed. (c) is worth doing regardless of (a)/(b) because it MEASURES how many existing citations are already dangling -- currently unknown, and unmeasured counts as zero.

THE NEXT DESIGN, AND WHY IT IS ROWED RATHER THAN RUN NOW: the standard remedy for anticipation is a GAPPED pre-window -- end the pre-period k days before the event so the anticipation zone is in neither leg -- with k pre-registered from the vesting-announcement lead time, not swept. Running it today would have been a FOURTH design chosen because the third refused, which is the garden of forking paths the three-design multiplicity charge exists to prevent; three nested designs each fixing a NAMED defect is a defensible sequence, a fourth chosen on a p-value is fishing. Pre-register k, charge the trial, and run it as its own study. NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: if the gapped design also refuses, that is a genuine finding about the ANTICIPATION channel and belongs in the graveyard with its number, not a reason for a fifth design.

MAX_AUDIT ACKS ARE GITIGNORED, SO A REPO-LEVEL DEFECT CAN NEVER BE ACKED WHERE IT PAGES. data/max_audit_acks.json is untracked (.gitignore data/*, and it carries none of the ! exceptions that data/decision_ledger.json, data/constitution_core.lock, data/gate0_signoff.json and 6 others do), and it has never appeared in git log. Acks are therefore PER-BOX. That is defensible for a runtime-state defect, whose truth genuinely differs per machine -- and wrong for a REPO-level one, whose truth is identical everywhere: prompt-doctrine-oversized is a property of a committed file, so acking it here leaves it firing on the VPS, where the doctrine's own escalation rule ('defects persisting >48h un-acked ESCALATE to the principal page') will page the principal for a defect that HAS a full reasoned disposition sitting in another checkout. That is the exact failure mode the ack mechanism exists to prevent, and it fires hardest on the desk's most carefully dispositioned items. max_audit already distinguishes RUNTIME from REPO scope internally (see the _fenced evidence-recording comment at scripts/max_audit.py:166 and the scope-aware tuple width at :6368), so the distinction needed to fix this is already computed and simply not applied to ack storage. FIX: split the ack file by scope -- REPO-scope acks tracked via a ! exception so they travel with the commit that reasons about them, RUNTIME-scope acks left local where they belong. Found while acking prompt-doctrine-oversized (R0391).

THE L1.29 CALIBRATION FENCE IS WELDED RED BY 44 FORECASTS ABOUT A SYMBOL THAT DOES NOT EXIST -- and R0367's fix, now committed, was necessary but NOT sufficient. Measured 2026-08-05: check_calibration.py reports OVERDUE with 44 forecasts past deadline; every one is the claim 'Will S2USDT trade ABOVE 102.0 in 24 hours time?'. S2USDT returns HTTP 400 from BOTH api.binance.com/api/v3/klines and fapi.binance.com/fapi/v1/klines while BTCUSDT returns rows from both, so the symbol is not delisted, it never existed -- 'S2' is a placeholder/hallucinated ticker (and 102.0 a placeholder price) emitted by the calibration probe. With R0367's alphabet fix in place score_forecasts.py now PARSES the symbol and reports '0 resolvable, 44 skipped -- no venue price for S2USDT', so the row moves from unparseable to unresolvable and the fence stays red either way. THIS IS THE EXPENSIVE DIRECTION: L1.29 exists because a Kelly bettor sized on over-confident estimates converges to ruin with probability one, and an ungraded forecast never counts its miss, so the measured hit-rate can only rise. A fence that can never go green gets ignored (L1.43), which disables the desk's only detector of being confidently wrong. TIES TO AN UNDISPOSED ROW: R0254 (undisposed 4.4d) already found this probe re-logs ONE identical claim 17x in 14h -- same probe, same claim; that is why the count is 44 rather than 1. FIX, TWO HALVES: (1) validate the symbol against a venue exchangeInfo AT LOG TIME so an unpriceable claim is refused rather than banked -- a forecast nothing can resolve is not a forecast; (2) dispose the existing 44 as UNRESOLVABLE-BY-CONSTRUCTION with the reason recorded, explicitly NOT as hits or misses, since scoring a placeholder either way corrupts the calibration term that feeds calibrated_confidence and from there Kelly leverage. Found while running the law gate for owed-work batch 3.

NO INSTRUMENT DETECTS A DAEMON RUNNING PRE-FIX CODE, and the desk has paid for that class repeatedly (institutional_knowledge: 'a committed fix is INERT until the process actually restarts'; the --hold-top churn fix sat dead 2 days). R0232 is the proving instance: it sat BLOCKED-OPERATOR for 4 days and then resolved itself silently by a restart nobody recorded -- no fence would have told the desk either way. verify_deployment.py answers the ARTIFACT question (is the output fresh) and is structurally blind to the CODE question: a daemon on 5-day-old code writes perfectly fresh artifacts. MEASURED NOW: executor PID 3424622 started 2026-08-05T11:47:22 while scripts/run_cashcarry_executor.py has mtime 13:18:31 and 3 commits (7cd7e18, 3bd2dd6, f632226) touched it after the process started -- the money-path daemon is on stale code AT THIS MOMENT and nothing reports it. Build scripts/check_code_deployed.py: per money-path daemon, process start via /proc/stat btime + /proc/pid/stat field 22 (NOT /proc mtime, which tracks ~now), walk the first-party import closure from the entry script, and fail when any imported source is newer than the process. UNOBSERVABLE must be its own status, distinct from CURRENT (a verdict about the HOST is not a verdict about the DESK).
recommendations.reason: IMPLEMENTED, AND THE ROW'S OWN PREMISE IS PARTLY RETRACTED -- I refuted it myself within the hour of writing it, which is the correction going on the record rather than being quietly dropped. The row claimed NO instrument detects a daemon on pre-fix code. FALSE: max_audit.check_stale_daemons (scripts/max_audit.py:540) has done exactly that since 2026-07-26, with a transitive import closure and systemd-independent worker discovery, and it is better designed than the new script I proposed. I asserted absence from a grep instead of reading the file -- desk lesson L0005, checkable in one command. THE REAL DEFECT WAS WORSE THAN THE ONE I ROWED, and only visible once the organ was read: the instrument existed, was well built, and COULD NOT FIRE. It took process start from Path('/proc/<pid>').stat().st_mtime, which tracks directory access rather than start, so it read 0.0167h for every polled daemon against true ages of 6.9h / 139.8h / 180.1h -- and 'files newer than started' with started ~= now can only match a file edited in the last minute. Zero recall, silently, on a class the desk has paid for three times. A missing detector announces itself; a welded one does not, so the retraction points at a MORE expensive defect, not a smaller one. Fixed in 38ec6e2 by upgrading the existing organ rather than adding the second one this row proposed (L2.9 upgrade-before-build): correct clock via /proc/stat btime + /proc/<pid>/stat field 22, verified against ps -o lstart= as an independent oracle. The fix also surfaced a second defect the row never anticipated -- with a correct clock the check immediately reported the Tier-3 RUIN RAIL as stale on a git-checkout mtime bump, so staleness is now judged on CONTENT (commit date for tracked-clean files, mtime only where git has no committed version). Measured: executor 2 changed files preserved as a true positive, deadman 1->0 and dashboard 1->0 as false positives removed. The row's UNOBSERVABLE-as-its-own-status point is now moot in this organ, which skips a daemon it cannot see rather than passing it.

recommendations.summary: TMPFS IS MEMORY THAT BELONGS TO NO PROCESS, AND NOTHING ON THIS DESK WATCHES IT. /tmp is a tmpfs, so pytest's tmp_path scratch is RESIDENT RAM on a 3.8GB swapless box carrying the live executor, three recorders and several agent sessions. Measured 2026-08-05: 35 orphaned pytest run dirs holding 1021MB (26% of the machine) against 189MB available; reclaiming took available to 1555MB. CLOSED LOOP, which is why it never self-corrected: an OOM-killed run never reaches its own cleanup, its stale lock makes pytest's GC skip the orphan, orphans accumulate, RAM falls, the next run is likelier to be killed. Prevention shipped (513ba24, tmp_path_retention_policy=failed) and the orphans cleared by hand. WHAT IS STILL OPEN AND IS THE REASON FOR THIS ROW: (a) no fence measures tmpfs occupancy or free RAM on this box at all -- every memory check watches PROCESS RSS, so this class is invisible by construction and 149MB of other stale /tmp artifacts remain uninspected; (b) max_audit's own _check_test_suite still mis-reads rc<0 as a collection error AND returns early past the test-suite-shrank ratchet, so a genuine suite shrink during a contended window is invisible -- deliberately not edited this cycle because scripts/max_audit.py was dirty under a concurrent session; (c) a whole-suite pytest verdict is STILL UNOBTAINED -- two full runs died and a batched run was in flight at cycle end, with one F sighted at 14% that has not been identified.

DESK-MEMORY OVERFLOW WILL BECOME A PERMANENTLY-RED FENCE, AND THE CAUSE IS A DESIGN TENSION NOBODY HAS PRICED. learn.py's docstring says graduation is the escape from saturation and that the lessons LEFT in the corpus are exactly the judgement calls a machine cannot make. But desk-memory-overflow fires on ANY un-graduated overflow. Those two statements cannot both hold at a FIXED 12000-char budget with a monotonically growing ledger: un-graduatable judgement-call lessons accumulate, and once their total exceeds the budget the fence is red forever through nobody's fault. That is a welded gate (L1.43) -- a fence that always fires carries zero information and gets acked into silence, which is how a real loss will hide. MEASURED 2026-08-05: 69 active lessons, 11528/12000 chars injected, 44 over budget, 43 graduated, 1 genuinely lost (L0068, cost=hygiene, a worktree-vs-env diagnostic procedure). recommendations.summary: NOTHING VERIFIES WHO WROTE THE CODE THIS BOX EXECUTES, AND THE WORKTREE GATE (R0246, 8c851e0) DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLOSE IT. Measured 2026-08-05: git log --format=%G? is 'N' for every commit in this repo, there is no allowed_signers file, and commit.gpgsign/gpg.format/user.signingkey are all unset. deploy/pull_deploy.sh runs from cron every 10 minutes on the box that owns data/secrets/binance_live.json, and gating a commit REQUIRES EXECUTING IT -- a worktree is not a sandbox. So an attacker who can push to origin (a compromised GitHub token is the whole attack) still gets arbitrary code execution as the quant user, because they control run_ci.py in the same commit and can simply make their own gate green. R0246 closed the ordering (the live tree, the pre-push hook it installs, the crontab it reconstitutes, and every supervised process that imports from the tree are no longer downstream of ungated code) and the ~10-min unvetted window. IT DID NOT CLOSE EXECUTION, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT: a security fix that oversells itself is worse than none, because the residual stops being tracked. THE ONLY CONTROL THAT STOPS EXECUTION is verifying the committer's SIGNATURE before running anything -- git verify-commit against a pinned allowed_signers, refusing the deploy on an unsigned or unknown-signer commit. AN ALLOWED-COMMITTER CHECK ON name/email IS WORTHLESS HERE and must not be built as a substitute: the committer fields are attacker-controlled by construction for anyone who can push. THIS NEEDS THE PRINCIPAL, which is why it is a row and not a commit: it requires provisioning a signing key (SSH-format is simplest, git config gpg.format ssh + user.signingkey + a committed allowed_signers), deciding which identities may deploy, and accepting that every future desk commit must be signed or the puller will refuse it -- a real operational commitment, not a code change. INTERIM MITIGATION AVAILABLE WITHOUT A KEY: scope the GitHub token to a deploy key with no push rights and push via a separate credential, which removes the single-token compromise path.
recommendations.reason: NEEDS THE PRINCIPAL, and that is the reason for the date rather than a commit. recommendations.summary: run_ci's IN-FLIGHT ATTRIBUTION SEES UNTRACKED FILES ONLY, SO A SIBLING EDITING AN EXISTING FILE STILL TURNS THE DESK-WIDE GATE RED. _inflight_py() runs git ls-files --others --exclude-standard: that is UNTRACKED files. A concurrent session MODIFYING A TRACKED FILE produces an empty in-flight list, _attribute returns every failure as committed-code, tracked_ok goes False and ci-gate-red fires naming a commit that is innocent. MEASURED 2026-08-05 20:5x: ruff reported 2 errors (E501 in libs/execution/carry_accounting.py:161 and tests/execution/test_carry_accounting.py:222, F841 in scripts/run_live_combined.py:135). All three files were ' M' -- a sibling's uncommitted money-path work. Committed HEAD linted CLEAN in a detached worktree. So the gate was red, the desk-wide alarm was firing, and there was NOTHING WRONG WITH ANY COMMIT. THIS IS THE EXACT FAILURE _attribute WAS BUILT FOR, LEFT HALF-DONE: its own docstring says those failures 'belong to NO COMMIT, the session that observes them cannot fix them, and they clear on their own', and that is equally true of a modified tracked file -- the implementation just never covered the case, and modified-tracked is the COMMON case for agents working an existing codebase. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE NOISE: run_ci.py:138 records that ci-gate-red recurred 8x in 10.7d and that fixing the instance bought exactly one cycle; a red everyone has learned to dismiss is how the genuine committed failure eb74f48 sat buried. THE FIX IS NOT TO WIDEN THE EXCLUSION LIST. Adding modified-tracked paths to the --ignore/--extend-exclude set would stop checking those files ENTIRELY, hiding a real committed error inside a file someone happens to be editing -- strictly worse. The right answer is the one R0246 just proved in deploy/pull_deploy.sh: GATE A DETACHED WORKTREE AT HEAD instead of judging the shared dirty tree, so the verdict is about a COMMIT by construction and needs no attribution heuristic at all. Note the worktree must have live data/ linked in per-entry or live-state tests pass for the wrong reason (desk lesson L0068), and it must share the CI lock -- both already solved in pull_deploy.sh and directly reusable.
recommendations.reason: run_ci in-flight attribution blind to tracked-file edits: real, recurring (ci-gate-red recurred 9x), and the fix is bounded -- extend the attribution snapshot to tracked dirty files via git status --porcelain instead of untracked-only. ABSORPTION COST IS HORIZON-DEPENDENT AND THE 1-YEAR FRAMING INVERTS ITS SIGN. Found by R0266's study (scripts/study_absorbing_kelly.py, docs/research/absorbing_kelly_study.json). Modelling absorption as the account FREEZING at the barrier -- correct for a venue minimum, since the money is still there -- floors terminal log-wealth at log(barrier) while the upside stays unbounded. Over a ONE-YEAR horizon that bounded downside makes E[logW] CONVEX in leverage once mu is uncertain: mu-dispersion pays like a call option, more spread puts more mass in the unbounded good tail while the bad tail is capped, and the measured optimum came out ABOVE full Kelly (f* 1.05 to 3.00). The first version of the study read that as 'the two shrinks double-count in 12/12 cells' and would have shipped a confident wrong number; it was caught only because a positive control and a no-barrier control were added. THE FIX IS THE HORIZON, NOT THE MODEL: this desk's objective is LIFETIME E[log W_T], and over a lifetime absorption forfeits ALL future compounding rather than settling at 0.2x book -- the very floor that creates the convexity is what a long horizon removes. WORK: re-run the study with multi-year horizons (or an explicit continuation value for the non-absorbed state) and confirm f*_joint falls below f*_absorbing as the horizon grows, which is the direction theory predicts. LOW PRIORITY and say so: the boundary shrink at the desk's real barrier measured <=10% (gamma_boundary 0.90-1.00 at the 00-on-k viability floor), an order of magnitude below the estimation shrink already applied, so nothing about deployed sizing turns on it. This row exists so the artifact's own caveat is tracked rather than living only in a docstring.

THE KELLY SHRINK IS THE RIGHT FORMULA WITH THE WRONG RATIONALE ATTACHED, AND THE TWO CALIBRATE DIFFERENTLY. Measured by R0266's study (CONTROL A, 12/12 cells): with an UNBIASED mu, estimation noise ALONE leaves the growth optimum at exactly full Kelly, f* = 1.00. That is not a simulation artifact -- E[log W_T] = T(L*mu - L^2 sigma^2/2) is LINEAR in mu, so averaging over symmetric unbiased parameter noise cannot move the argmax. The rationale carried in libs/risk/kelly_shrink.py and echoed in the constitution -- 'Kelly's penalty is asymmetric, so shrinkage RAISES expected log growth on an estimated edge' -- does not survive that test: the asymmetry is already inside the quadratic term, and symmetric noise about a correct mean does not shift the optimum. THE SHRINK IS STILL CORRECT, and this row must not be read as an argument to bet more. What justifies it is that mu-hat is NOT unbiased for the quantity the desk bets on: candidates are selected BECAUSE they measured well, so mu-hat carries a winner's curse, and the correct input is the POSTERIOR MEAN under a prior that most candidates have no edge. S^2/(S^2+SE^2) is exactly the James-Stein / normal-posterior shrinkage factor toward a zero-edge prior, so the FORM is right. WHY IT MATTERS PRACTICALLY: the two stories calibrate differently. A posterior-mean shrink should be tuned to (a) how strong the zero-edge prior is -- this desk has 420 tested / 0 survivors of evidence for a very strong one -- and (b) how SELECTED the particular candidate was, i.e. how many trials it won against. Neither is an input today; the shrink sees only S and N, so it applies the same haircut to an edge picked from 1 trial and one picked from 420, when the winner's curse differs enormously between them. WORK: restate the docstring rationale, then decide whether to feed the trial count (already tracked for DSR multiplicity) into the shrink. Direction of any change is TIGHTER for heavily-selected candidates, never looser.
